2. Heard Sri Anil Kumar Verma, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh,
learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.108 of 2024, under Sections 376, 511, 386 I.P.C., Section 17 POCSO Act and Section 67A I.T. Act, Police Station Badagaon, District Varanasi, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant and co-accused person Deepak are stated to have made an indecent video of the daughter of the informant in a compromising state with co-accused person Sanjay vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191932862/
1 Shashipal and is stated to have made it viral on social media, which was seen by the informant in the mobile of the applicant and the co-accused person himself.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

The indecent video,
if any, has been recovered from the mobile of the informant himself.
It has not been found being made viral on social media, as such, it has not been recovered from the mobile of any other person.
Learned counsel has further stated that even the said video, being perused by the Investigating Officer, does not indicate whether the victim and the co-accused person are clearly visible in it.
It is stated that there was darkness at that time, as such, the victim and the co-accused person are not clearly visible in it.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that there is no evidence about the date on which the applicant is stated to have transferred the said indecent video to the mobile of the informant, as such, it is a clear-cut case of false implication.
Learned counsel has further stated that as per ossification test report, the age of the victim was found between seventeen and half years to eighteen and half years.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 02.04.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. LearnedState Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant- Sanjay, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
